describes: Surface cues for lowering free text into the deontic language, as DATA — sufficient on its own for a generic consumer (the ingest plane) to extract deterministically without importing any deontic code. deontic's own reference producer, deontic.prose (used by the plane descriptor), does NOT read this file at runtime: Phase 1 replaced the regex walk with a stdlib recursive-descent parser (deontic.prose_grammar) driven by the JSON gazetteers under artifacts/gazetteer/*.json — that parser's single source of cues. This file stays the single, self-sufficient surface for a consumer that does not want to import deontic code at all, and tools/check_extraction.py's gazetteer-sync gate holds every gazetteer-published cue (modal phrases, negation adverbs, negating interposed phrases, condition leads/tails, exception leads) equal to (covered by) this file's regex, so the two published surfaces cannot drift apart. The regex sources here are also held equal to the language modules (deontic.incidents) by tools/check_extraction.py; the modal cues (surface phrase -> modal class) are the one piece the package deliberately does not carry in code, published here for consumers. The deadline_cues, cross_reference_cues, and sanction_cues are additive: they populate the optional carry fields (deadline / cross_references / sanction) added to statement.schema.json; like the modal cues they are published as data only, carried nowhere in code (opaque text the reasoning layer types, resolves, and applies). Each named group holds the extracted value; the FULL match is the cue's published surface (a consumer that records or removes the surface anchors on the full match, so the clause-level deadline entries deliberately cover the whole deadline clause — connective, feasibility qualifier, cue, value, reference-point tail — while the named group still holds only the value). The validity_cues lower CONSTITUTIVE validity norms (a term 'is void' / 'ist unwirksam' directs no conduct; it denies legal effect): each cue carries an effect (void / preserved / substitution), and validity_rules maps an effect to the Hohfeldian incident borne by the norm's addressee — void is the drafter's disability to give the term legal effect (the counterparty's immunity follows via the published correlatives); preserved and substitution abstain ('') as consequence shapes with no single addressee incident. Validity is NOT a fourth modal operator: the operator set stays O/P/F, and validity lives in the constitutive/incident layer the language already publishes. slot_cues.condition_tail lifts a trailing condition clause ('before it is sent') into the condition slot, mirroring the gazetteer-driven parser's own condition_tail production (artifacts/gazetteer/condition.json's tail_leads); where the trailing phrase is not a clause ('after use') deontic.prose abstains rather than choose between condition and adverbial. Round 4 (deontic-is-ought correction): this file publishes no operator->5D binding; the earlier operator_axis key is removed. Operators (O/P/F) are ought; the 5D describes what is; a norm's content enters 5D through the factual plane, not through the operator. deontic.contract.dimension_affinity and deontic.plane.binding are total functions that answer with no dimension for any operator. Round 5 defect (a), generalised: a negation adverb after a modal ("not", "never", "at no time"), with or without interposed commas or an interposed phrase (e.g. "shall never, under any circumstances,"), lowers the modal to F (prohibition), with the negation adverb and any interposed phrase consumed by the matched cue so neither reaches `action` nor is duplicated onto `negated` — the same convention "must not"/"shall not" already carry. slot_cues.condition_lead covers 'if'/'where'/'when'/'provided that'/'subject to'/'in the event of', each sentence-initial, stripped from the published condition; condition_lead stays sentence-initial-only by design (a lead phrase appearing after the modal is not lifted into condition — see deontic.prose_grammar.analyze's documented grammar, condition as a sibling constituent of modal_frame, never nested inside it). 'in the case of' is NOT a condition lead: it is a genuine condition on some real text but a bare scope/topic marker with no conditional force on other real text, and the surface alone cannot tell the two apart — an ambiguous lead is not consumed (see artifacts/gazetteer/condition.json's describes for the worked examples). slot_cues.condition_lead_with_phrase covers 'at the request of'/'upon the request of'/'in such a case': its named group captures the lead's own words AS PART OF the condition, because stripping the lead would either lose the request itself ('at the request of the data subject' is a request, not only a party) or, for the anaphoric 'in such a case', publish an EMPTY condition indistinguishable from an unconditional duty (see deontic.prose_grammar's keep_lead mechanism, same gazetteer entries, artifacts/gazetteer/condition.json). slot_cues.exception_lead does NOT include 'by way of derogation from' or 'abweichend von': 'by way of derogation from X, R' means R OVERRIDES X — R is the exception to X, not the other way round — so modelling it as this rule's OWN exception would invert the relation; it is not modelled as anything else either (see artifacts/gazetteer/exception.json's describes). The pre-existing bare 'abweichend' alternative here is UNCHANGED and stays a known, out-of-scope issue (it captures an entire German main rule as if it were an exception on the regex surface). incident_cues.power_verb is word-anchored to explicit finite-verb forms wherever a bare stem+\w* wildcard also spelled an unrelated common noun/adjective: elect\w* matched "electronic"/"election"/"elector"/"electoral"; withdraw\w* matched "withdrawal"; waive\w* matched "waiver"; approv\w* matched "approval"; authoris\w*/authoriz\w* matched "authorisation"/"authorization"; assign\w* matched "assignment"/"assignable"; renew\w* matched "renewal"; instruct\w* matched "instruction(s)"/"instructor". Each of those eight is now anchored to its explicit finite-verb inflections (irregular ones spelled out, e.g. withdraw/withdraws/withdrawing/withdrew/withdrawn) instead of stem+\w*; "authorised"/"authorized" is additionally excluded immediately before "representative(s)" (a defined role, not an exercised power). terminat\w*/rescind\w*/revoke\w*/consent\w*/suspend\w* were checked and found with no such collision (left unchanged); exercis\w* is left unchanged on purpose ("exercise" is the identical spelling for the noun and the verb in English — no word-anchoring can separate them); the German stems are also left unchanged (German nominalises most of them with the same stem+"-ung" pattern, and two are zero-derivation like "exercise" — see deontic.incidents._POWER_VERBS's own comment for the full account). "require" is deliberately NOT a power_verb regex alternative: a permission to require something of another party is a Hohfeldian power, but only the exact active forms "require"/"requires"/"requiring" count — never any form of "required", since a passive or reduced-relative "required" ("as required under Article 6", "information required to assess compliance") has no reliable surface cue separating it from an active one — and the check runs over the action span ONLY, never the whole raw sentence. This is published as structured DATA below, require_power_cue, that a generic consumer can apply by plain word membership without importing any deontic code or compiling a regex, held equal to deontic.incidents._has_active_require's own constants by tools/check_extraction.py, and wired into incident_rules (when_matches: "require_power_cue") so the published rules surface reproduces classify_incident's "require" reading, not only its power_verb reading. classify_incident's modal=="obligation" branch returns "duty" before ever consulting power_verb or require_power_cue, so "require" inside an obligation's own action text is never misread as a power/disability.

modal_cues.pattern: \b(?:shall not|must not|may not|(?:shall|must|may)(?:\s*,\s*|\s+)(?:never|at\s+no\s+time)\s*,?\s*(?:[^,.;]+?,\s*)?|is not permitted to|is prohibited from|darf\s+\w+\s+nicht|darf nicht)\b
\b(?:shall|must|is obliged to|is required to|has to|muss|m(?:ü|u)ssen|hat zu)\b
\b(?:may|is permitted to|is free to|is entitled to|is authorised to|darf|kann)\b

slot_cues.condition_lead_with_phrase: ^\s*(?P<cond>(?:at the request of|upon the request of|in such a case)\b.*?),
slot_cues.exception_lead: \b(?:unless|except|save where|save as|without prejudice to|es sei denn|abweichend)\b\s*(?P<exc>.*)$

require_power_cue.describes: A permission/right to require something of another party is a Hohfeldian power (classify_incident -> 'power'), and the removal of that power under a prohibition is a disability — but only the exact active forms below, applied to the ACTION span only, never the whole raw sentence. Mirrors deontic.incidents._has_active_require and skills/deontic/deontic_engine._has_active_require exactly, and is wired into incident_rules below (when_matches: 'require_power_cue') so the published rules surface reproduces the same reading.

cross_reference_cues.instrument: \b(?:in accordance with|pursuant to|as (?:set out|referred to|provided|specified) in|under|subject to|gem(?:ä|a)(?:ß|ss)|nach|im Sinne (?:des|der))\s+(?P<ref>(?:Article|Art\.?|Section|Sec\.?|§|Regulation|Directive|Annex|Artikel|Absatz|Abs\.?|Anhang)\s*[\w.()/\-]+)

sanction_cues.lead: \b(?:on pain of|under penalty of|subject to (?:a\s+)?(?:penalty|fine|sanction)|shall be (?:liable|punishable)|punishable by|liable to (?:a\s+)?(?:fine|penalty)|unter Androhung|bei (?:Androhung|Strafe|Vermeidung))\b(?P<sanction>[^.]*)
